What this product is allowed to count, and exactly what may travel with each thing counted. It is a list rather than a convention because a convention is a thing people mean to follow: an event not named here is dropped, and a property not named under its event is stripped before anything sees it. That makes 'we do not collect that' a fact about the code rather than a promise in a policy.

Three rules the shape of this file enforces.

No free text, ever. The journey builder has a box a visitor types a sentence into — 'twelve days in September, wildlife and mountains' — and the obvious mistake is to record it. Every value permitted below is an enum the dataset already contains (a lens key, a country slug, a month number, a pacing key) or a small integer. There is nowhere for a sentence to go, and a test asserts it.

No identifiers. No cookie, no localStorage id, no fingerprint, no IP-derived anything, nothing that survives a reload or joins two page-loads together. These are counts of what happened, not a trail of who did it.

Nothing leaves the browser by default. There is no third-party script and no endpoint. Until somebody sets a sink, `track()` validates the event and returns; the events exist so that the day a destination is chosen it is one line, and so that the choice is visible rather than inherited from a tag manager.

$props.wants: how many lenses were chosen — a count, not which
$props.stages: how many stages the journey has
$props.source: how the builder was entered: link, sentence, questions, atlas
